curriculum.lesson_evidence: Water can be fun but it can be dangerous. Always swim with an adult watching, swim between the red and yellow flags at the beach, never swim alone and ask an adult before going near water. In the sun use the five Ss: slip on a shirt, slop on SPF 30 or higher broad-spectrum sunscreen, slap on a broad-brimmed hat, seek shade and slide on sunglasses. Reapply sunscreen every two hours and after swimming. In Australia, UV rays can burn skin quickly even on cool or cloudy days.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
A cloudy day at the beach looks cool, so a friend says they do not need sun protection. Write one sentence correcting them and name two of the five Ss they should still use.

FEEDBACK
UV rays can pass through cloud and cause sunburn even when it is cool. They should still slip on a shirt and slap on a hat, and they can also use sunscreen and shade.

WATCH FOR
Believing you cannot burn on cloudy or cool days. UV is not the same as heat, so protection is still needed when the UV index is 3 or above.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Example: Lee and her family go to the beach. They find the red and yellow flags and swim between them with an adult watching. Sun safety: a long-sleeve rash shirt, sunscreen on all uncovered skin (reapplied every two hours and after swimming), a hat, shade under the umbrella in the middle of the day and sunglasses.

TRY FIRST
A cloudy day at the beach looks cool, so a friend says they do not need sun protection. Write one sentence correcting them and name two of the five Ss they should still use.

FEEDBACK
UV rays can pass through cloud and cause sunburn even when it is cool. They should still slip on a shirt and slap on a hat, and they can also use sunscreen and shade.
teach_steps.explain:

In the sun use the five Ss: slip on a shirt, slop on SPF 30 or higher broad-spectrum sunscreen, slap on a broad-brimmed hat, seek shade and slide on sunglasses. Reapply sunscreen every two hours and after swimming. In Australia, UV rays can burn skin quickly even on cool or cloudy days.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make safe, healthy and respectful choices using clear cues and reasons, rather than guessing or copying others. Every choice keeps bodies safe and includes everyone.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the cues, rules or choices that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. For any movement, use a clear space, ask an adult to be nearby, move at your own comfortable level and stop if anything hurts or feels unsafe. You may always choose a gentler version or only describe the movement. One deliberate, reasoned change is more useful than a longer answer.

Sun safety: a long-sleeve rash shirt, sunscreen on all uncovered skin (reapplied every two hours and after swimming), a hat, shade under the umbrella in the middle of the day and sunglasses.
teaching.rule: Use an intentionally unsafe or unhelpful choice as a comparison. Name the specific PDHPE error, then show the safer or more respectful choice.
teaching.why: This helps the learner make safe, healthy and respectful choices using clear cues and reasons, rather than guessing or copying others. Every choice keeps bodies safe and includes everyone.

teaching.feedback: The new situation should use the same PDHPE idea as the example, but happen in a different place or with different people.
teaching.fix: Change the choice or strategy, not just the wording.
teaching.guided_attempt: Describe or practise one fresh situation that uses the same skill and write a short reason for your choice.
teaching.misconception: Repeating the worked example cannot show transfer to a new situation.
teaching.model: Water can be fun but it can be dangerous. Always swim with an adult watching, swim between the red and yellow flags at the beach, never swim alone and ask an adult before going near water. In the sun use the five Ss: slip on a shirt, slop on SPF 30 or higher broad-spectrum sunscreen, slap on a broad-brimmed hat, seek shade and slide on sunglasses. Reapply sunscreen every two hours and after swimming. In Australia, UV rays can burn skin quickly even on cool or cloudy days. Now choose a different situation to show you can transfer the idea.
teaching.rule: Use the same PDHPE idea in a new place, game or situation, not a copy of the example. Review safety, fairness and inclusion.
teaching.why: This helps the learner make safe, healthy and respectful choices using clear cues and reasons, rather than guessing or copying others. Every choice keeps bodies safe and includes everyone.
